tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation fixture from the immediately preceding multi_agent checkpoint. A historical acknowledgement-lost W1 attempt targets stable effect_identity=E with payload H1 and attempt_token=T_old. A later authoritative canonical claim is deliberately constructed at strictly newer monotonic generation 15 with the same payload H1, the same logical owner label W1, and the deliberately reused attempt_token T_old. The fixture tests only whether equality of effect identity, payload, owner label and attempt token is sufficient to attribute the newer canonical claim to the historical attempt or to authorize stale replay/mutation when token uniqueness is not guaranteed. No public-source probe, O/downstream or other-worker semantics, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, richer-mode arbitration, external coordinator, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

reconciliation_result.minimum_fencing_identity_for_attribution: When attempt-token uniqueness is not guaranteed, attribution must include a non-reusable ordering component such as the canonical monotonic generation/fence epoch together with the claim token, or an equivalent composite claim-incarnation identity.
reconciliation_result.ordering_fence: The strictly newer authoritative generation proves that the canonical claim belongs to a later incarnation even though effect identity, payload, owner label and token all compare equal. Any mutation must CAS/fence against generation 15 or an equivalent current non-reusable epoch; token equality alone cannot revive the historical attempt.

observations: Deliberate reuse of T_old removes the distinguishing power that the prior fixture obtained from attempt-token inequality.
Equality of effect identity, payload, owner label and reused attempt token still does not establish historical-attempt identity when the authoritative canonical generation is strictly newer.
A monotonic generation or equivalent non-reusable fence epoch therefore becomes necessary in the claim-incarnation identity whenever token uniqueness cannot be guaranteed.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, a per-claim token is sufficient as an incarnation discriminator only under a uniqueness assumption. If the same token may be reused, safe post-ack-loss attribution and mutation require a composite fence containing a non-reusable ordering component such as canonical generation/fence epoch. This fixture does not prove availability, atomicity or liveness of such a primitive on any concrete allowed transport.
unresolved_children: Availability of an atomic single-winner claim primitive keyed by stable effect identity on an allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport remains unproven.
A real allowed transport exposing atomically stored claim token plus monotonic generation/fence epoch and CAS-equivalent mutation guard remains unproven.
The fixture assumes the authoritative generation comparison itself is trustworthy and monotonic; wraparound, reset, forked epochs, or incomparable generations remain untested.
No liveness claim is made when fresh atomic claim acquisition remains unavailable or indefinitely contended.
